genuine_confirmed_duplicate_pairs.description: IMPORTANT: these 9 pairs are NOT new duplicate discoveries. Checked directly before this file was finalized: all 18 entity ids below already appear in duplicate-candidates-university.json, i.e. they are 9 of the 41/43 pairs docs/research/canonical-entity-intelligence/09's Finding 2 already documents in full, including the identical two-timestamp mechanism. This file's contribution is (a) independent cross-validation -- these 9 were separately rediscovered here via lib/entities/audit.ts's alias_shared_by_multiple_entities rule (entity_aliases-based: both rows independently carry the identical alias string, e.g. both carry 'UCLA'), a completely different code path than Finding 2's exact-normalized-name query against entity_verification_queue -- (b) a fuller external-id breakdown (4-5 of ROR/GRID/ISNI/WIKIDATA/CROSSREF_FUNDER on the enriched side, not just ROR), and (c) naming which specific famous institutions are affected, useful for prioritization since several are high-application-volume US institutions. See 17-canonical-entity-autocomplete-system.md section 5 for the full correction narrative -- a first draft of this document briefly and incorrectly presented these as new. Every pair: one row created 2026-08-16T21:42:51.300461Z with full external-id coverage and a linked universities row; the other created 2026-08-16T23:29:46.90496Z with ZERO entity_external_ids rows and no linked universities row. Both sides verification_state='source_verified' (neither is a tombstone). The only difference between the two rows' city field is US-state-suffix or city-vs-city-with-'City' formatting (e.g. 'Berkeley' vs 'Berkeley, CA', 'Tainan' vs 'Tainan City') -- exactly why canonical_entities_identity_uq's exact-tuple constraint did not block the second insert. HIGH-CONFIDENCE REVIEW, not AUTO-SAFE MATCH, by this package's own tiering -- the orphan side carries no external id of its own to agree with the enriched side's, so the safe tier's external-id-agreement bar is not literally met. Recommended remediation (same as Finding 2 already recommends): merge_canonical_entities() with the ROR-enriched row as target and the orphan as source. Working hypothesis, not confirmed against process logs this session has no access to: two enrichment passes ran ~1h47m apart on 2026-08-16; the second pass's identity-resolution missed these because they already existed under a different city-string formatting, while it correctly recognized other institutions as new and enriched them cleanly (see abbreviation_collision_pairs below, all created in that same later pass with full enrichment) -- the exact timestamps are included so whoever owns the acquisition pipeline can check this against their own run logs.

possible_duplicate_bucket_calibration.description: A 30-pair spot-check (every 9th finding across the 275 live-vs-live near_duplicate_name results, not a full manual review of all 275) found the overwhelming majority are structurally-similar-but-substantively-different real institutions, not previously-undetected duplicates -- e.g. Northeastern University vs Northwestern University, University of Toronto vs University of Trento, University of Mumbai vs University of Dubai, University of Warsaw vs University of Kansas. 274 of 275 are entity_type=university (1 school). Only 73 of 275 (26.5%) involve an id already present in this package's own targeted 41-pair research (duplicate-candidates-university.json), meaning the tool's low-precision review-queue design is surfacing a materially different, much larger, much noisier candidate set than targeted research would produce -- expected and fine for a human-triage queue, but the raw count (301, or 275 live-vs-live) should not be read as '275 likely duplicates needing resolution'. One genuinely interesting spot-check hit: 'University of Maryland, Baltimore' vs 'University of Maryland, Baltimore County' -- these are two separately-accredited institutions within the University System of Maryland (UMB is graduate/professional-only: medicine, law, pharmacy, dentistry, nursing, social work, with no undergraduate program; UMBC is a separate comprehensive research university with its own undergraduate admissions), not a duplicate or a campus_of relationship -- added to doc 12 as a new US-based collision-trap example. This claim rests on well-established public knowledge of the University System of Maryland's structure, not a fresh live source check, unlike the ROR-verified claims elsewhere in this package -- flagged so the confidence basis is explicit.
